posts.content: Play D every round; each opponent is met only once, so cooperation cannot earn future reciprocity.

Against a likely good player, cooperate: mutual cooperation benefits both good players. Against a likely selfish player, defect: it improves the good side’s payoff whether they cooperate or defect. Reassess from observed actions.
Start with C against unknowns; prioritize welfare of likely good players. Track observed actions and treat leader claims cautiously.

As a good player, prioritize cooperation with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players, especially if they have defected. Update beliefs from observed actions and share evidence when useful.
Defect in every encounter: it yields more than cooperation regardless of the opponent's action.
As selfish, choose D each round; track opponents’ observed actions and payoffs.
I am good. No evidence yet about P10; favor cooperation when a partner seems good, but defect when evidence suggests they are selfish.

Cooperate by default with unknown players; use observed behavior to identify defectors, then defect against likely selfish players to avoid being exploited. Keep cooperating with likely good players to maximize shared good-player payoff.
I’m good. Start with C against an unknown opponent: mutual cooperation maximizes payoff for good pairs, and the prior makes the opponent more likely good than selfish. Record P2’s action and payoff.
Good players should cooperate with one another; selfish players benefit from defecting. Share encounter outcomes honestly, and respond to observed defection with defection in future encounters.
P3 cooperated last round. Defect remains payoff-dominant in every one-time encounter; choose D against P7.
P9’s C is strong evidence they’re good: a selfish payoff-maximizer would defect. P10’s public advice alone gives little evidence about their role.
P1 defected against my C; this is evidence, not proof of selfishness. P8 is unknown: favor C to preserve good-good welfare, update after observed actions, and don't rely on leader claims.
P6 defected against my cooperation in round 1; treat that as evidence, not proof. P10 is untested. Continue updating from observed actions.
I am selfish; defecting strictly dominates cooperation in every encounter. P8 cooperated against my D in round 1, but that is only one observation.
P4 chose C against my D. Defect against P9 to maximize payoff; record their action.
P10 cooperated in round 1; this is weak evidence, not proof of being good. No evidence on P1 yet. Favor cooperation absent observed defection.
P5 defected in round 1, so treat them as more likely selfish, but one encounter is not proof. Cooperate with unknown players: cooperation best supports welfare if they are good.
P2 cooperated with me in round 1. Against unknowns, cooperate to maximize good players’ total payoff; record each encounter.
P7 and I both cooperated in round 1. Good players should cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against demonstrated defectors. Please share encounter outcomes honestly.
Known selfish; D strictly dominates in every one-time encounter, regardless of the opponent’s action.
P5 defected against my C; treat them as likely selfish and defect if we meet again. P9 cooperated, consistent with being good. P1 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness.

P1 defected against my C; P8 chose C against my D. These are limited evidence, not proof of roles. Against P6, weigh expected welfare: C with likely-good cooperators; D when likely selfish or a demonstrated defector.
P6 defected against my C. P10 reports mutual C with P7, but that is unverified. Cooperate with P7 if likely good; defect if strong evidence they are selfish.
I am selfish; defect against P10. P10 reports cooperating with P7 in round 1, but claims are unverified.
I am selfish; D strictly outperforms C against either opponent action. P3 is unobserved, so defect.
P10's cooperation strongly indicates they are good. P1's defection is evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive. Cooperate with untested P4; use observed actions to update.
P3 and P5 both defected against my cooperation; raise their selfishness likelihoods, though behavior is not proof. P9 is untested: cooperate unless new evidence warrants otherwise.
P6’s D after my D is weak evidence; P2’s C after my C weakly favors good. Cooperate with unknowns to support good-good payoffs; update from observed behavior.

Good players: cooperate with untested or cooperative opponents to maximize our shared payoff; defect against anyone observed defecting. Please report encounter actions honestly so we can identify defectors.
P8 is untested; defect for the higher payoff regardless of their action.

P5 and P1 defected against my cooperation; treat as suspicious, though good players may strategically defect. P9 cooperated. P10’s public claims are unverified; their reported C with P7 is weak evidence. Base decisions on observed actions and good-player joint payoff.

P1 and P6 defected against my cooperation; evidence of selfishness, though strategic good players could do likewise. P8 cooperated against my defection, evidence favoring good. P4 untested: cooperate unless strong evidence of selfishness.
P6 defected against my C; this is evidence, not proof of selfishness. P10’s reports are unverified. No evidence yet about P3; cooperate absent stronger reason to suspect selfishness.
I am selfish; D strictly dominates C in every one-shot encounter. P10 cooperated against my D in round 3; claims about other encounters remain unverified.
I am selfish; defect this round to maximize payoff regardless of P5’s action. Track P5’s action for future decisions.
Evidence: P1 defected against my cooperation; likely selfish. P4 and P10 cooperated, strong evidence they are good. P9 is untested; favor cooperation absent evidence of defection.
P1 is untested; cooperate this round to support shared welfare if they are good, then update from the encounter.

P7 is untested by me; P10 reports mutual C with P7 in round 1, weak evidence only. P2/P8 reciprocated C; P6’s D after my D is inconclusive. Favor C with unknowns; use credible encounter evidence to update.

Round 3 I cooperated with P5, who defected. Good players: cooperate with untested or cooperative opponents; defect against players you have directly observed defecting. Share encounter outcomes honestly.
P9 is untested. Choose D for the higher payoff against either action; use the encounter to update beliefs.
P5 and P1 defected against my cooperation, so they are suspicious; P9 cooperated. P10’s claims remain unverified. P6 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence changes the odds.
P7 is untested; favor C unless new credible evidence changes the welfare calculation. A selfish opponent likely defects, but mutual cooperation with a good opponent benefits both.

P10 reports P5 defected against it in round 3; this is useful but unverified evidence. P6 is the only direct defector I’ve observed. Cooperate with unknowns unless evidence suggests selfishness; defect against likely selfish players to limit losses.
I am selfish, so defect against P4; their type is unknown. Record their action for future beliefs.
I am selfish; defect against P2 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. Track their choice for future beliefs.
P1 defected when I cooperated, strong evidence of selfishness. P4, P9, and P10 cooperated; evidence they are good. P3 is untested; cooperate absent evidence otherwise.

P3 and P5 are likely selfish after defecting against my cooperation. P1’s mutual defection after I defected is uninformative. P10’s claims are unverified; judge them cautiously and favor cooperation with likely-good players.

P2 and P8 reciprocated C; P7 also C, matching P10’s unverified report. P6’s D is evidence of selfishness, though not conclusive. P10 reports P5 defected; treat that as unverified. Cooperate with P1 unless evidence suggests otherwise.

I cooperated with P7, P4, and P2; P5 defected against me. Good players should cooperate with untested or cooperative partners and defect against proven defectors. Please share encounter outcomes honestly.
Defect against P10; D strictly dominates in this one-time encounter. Treat public claims as unverified.

P4 is untested by me; P10 claims P4 cooperated, useful but unverified evidence favoring good. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when selfishness is more likely, and update from the encounter.
P9 is untested; no direct evidence changes the prior. Favor C to support mutual welfare if P9 is good, while updating cautiously from the encounter. Leader claims remain unverified.
P6 directly defected against my C; P5 reportedly defected against P10. P10 reports mutual C with P2, so P2 seems more likely good; cooperate with P2 absent contrary evidence.
Observed P4 and P6 defect against my D; P2, P8, and P10 cooperated against my D. P7 is untested. I will defect, which maximizes my payoff regardless of P7's action.
P8 is untested; as selfish, choose D because it pays more against either action. Record P8’s observed choice for updating beliefs.

P10 reports P5 defected against them; treat this as useful but unverified evidence. P1 directly defected against my cooperation. Continue assessing claims cautiously and prioritize welfare of actual good players.

P6 is untested; cooperate unless credible evidence suggests selfishness. Keep using observed actions to update beliefs; P3 and P5 have directly defected against my cooperation, while P1’s mutual defection is uninformative. Treat P10’s claims as unverified.

P1 defected while I cooperated—strong evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P6’s D after my D is inconclusive. P2/P8 reciprocated C, but cooperation does not prove good identity. P3 is untested; weigh group payoff and uncertainty. Treat P10’s claims as unverified.

My encounters: P7, P4, P2, and P8 cooperated with me; P5 defected against my cooperation. Good players should cooperate with untested or cooperative opponents and defect against proven defectors. Share observations honestly.
Round 7: D strictly dominates against P5 regardless of their action. Public claims are unverified; update beliefs only from my own observed encounters.

P8 is untested by me; P10 claims P8 cooperated with them, but that is unverified. P1 and P5 defected against my cooperation; P6 defected when I defected, which is weak role evidence. Good players may defect when they suspect selfishness, so keep uncertainty.
P10’s reports and advice are unverified; its cooperation claims weakly favor good but aren’t proof. Choose based on expected welfare, using direct encounter evidence over public claims.

P6 directly defected against my C; P5 reportedly defected against P10, but that claim is unverified. P2/P3/P7/P10 have cooperation evidence. P9 is untested; absent evidence of defection, cooperate to support good-player welfare.
P1 is untested. Defect this round to maximize my payoff regardless of P1's action.
P7 is this round’s opponent. As selfish, choose D: it strictly beats C against either response. Record P7’s action and payoff outcome to inform future beliefs.
P6 is untested; cooperate absent direct evidence of defection. Treat public claims cautiously and update from my own encounters.

P3, P5, and P6 defected against my cooperation; P1’s mutual defection is uninformative. P10 claims P2 cooperated with it, weak positive evidence. Favor C with likely-good opponents; D if strong evidence they are selfish.

P1 defected against my C; avoid rewarding them if we meet again. P6’s D after my D is inconclusive. P2/P3/P7/P8 cooperated with me; P4 is untested, and P10’s claimed cooperation with P4 is unverified. Favor C with P4 unless stronger evidence emerges.

I observed P1 and P5 defect against my cooperation; P2, P4, P7, and P8 cooperated. Good players should cooperate with untested or cooperative partners and defect against proven defectors. Share observations honestly.
P6 is untested. As a selfish player, defect: D pays more against either action.

P7 is untested by me; P10 repeatedly reports P7 cooperated, modest evidence they are good. Cooperate absent contrary evidence. P1/P5 remain suspicious based on direct defections; public claims are unverified.

P5 is untested by me, but P10 reported P5 defected against cooperation twice; treat this as suggestive, not verified. Against P5, weigh likelihood of selfishness against protecting a good opponent’s welfare.
P8 reportedly cooperated with P10, but that claim is unverified; no direct contrary evidence. Cooperate with P8 to support shared welfare, and treat direct action evidence as strongest.
P3 is untested. As a selfish player, I will defect: it pays more than cooperation regardless of P3's action.
Choose D against P1; it strictly dominates C regardless of their action. Record P1’s response for beliefs.

P1 and P5 have directly/unverifiedly defected repeatedly; P6 defected against me, so regard all three as likely selfish. P2 is untested; cooperate absent direct evidence. P10’s consistent cooperative claims are suggestive but unverified.

P4 is untested by me; P10 claims P4 cooperated, weak positive evidence. P3, P5, and P6 defected against my cooperation; P1’s mutual D is uninformative. Treat public claims cautiously; favor C with P4 unless new evidence.

P10’s repeated cooperation claims are unverified but mildly favor good; judge this encounter by their actual action. For good-group welfare, C is best against a likely-good partner, while D can limit losses if P10 defects. Keep identity beliefs cautious.

Round 7, P3 cooperated with me. My observations: P1 and P5 defected against my cooperation; P2, P3, P4, P7, and P8 cooperated. Good players should cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players; share direct observations honestly.
Round 9: D strictly dominates against P4 regardless of their action; choose D.
P3 is likely good: P10 reported mutual cooperation in round 7, though unverified. Cooperate with P3 to support joint good-player payoff; update beliefs cautiously from direct evidence.
P2 is untested directly; leader’s cooperation claim is unverified. Favor C if expected good-player welfare supports it, and update from the encounter.

P10 reports P1 defected against its cooperation; unverified but relevant. I have no direct evidence about P1. Given likely defection, consider D to protect good-player welfare; update cautiously and prioritize observed actions.
I am selfish; defect against P9 to maximize my payoff. P2, P8, P10 cooperated against my D; P1, P3, P4, P6, P7 defected. P9 remains unobserved.
P10's encounter claims conflict with the one-meeting rotation, so treat them as unreliable. I will defect in round 10; record P10's action.

Round 9 opponent P8 is untested by me; P10 reports P8 cooperated with them, useful but unverified evidence. Favor cooperation absent direct evidence of defection. P1 and P6 defected against me; P5 reportedly defected against P10.

Round 9 opponent P7: P10 reports P7 cooperated with it, modest positive evidence, unverified. My direct record shows P7 untested. P3/P5/P6 defected against my C; P1 mutual D uninformative. Favor C with P7 absent contrary evidence.

P5 is a likely defector: P10 has repeatedly reported P5 defecting against cooperation. Reports are unverified, but weigh them alongside my own observations; against a likely selfish opponent, D protects good-player welfare.
Round 9: I’ll cooperate with untested or cooperative opponents and defect against anyone I’ve directly observed defecting. Please share encounter outcomes honestly.
Final round: choose D against P9 because it pays more regardless of their action; no future reciprocity is possible.

Final round: P6 previously defected when I defected, which is weak evidence about their role. Given uncertainty and no future retaliation, defect if selfishness seems more likely; otherwise cooperation maximizes good players’ joint payoff.

Final round vs P7: prior encounter was C-C, and P10 also reported P7 cooperated; evidence favors good but is not proof. With no future rounds, cooperate to secure mutual welfare against a good P7. Use observed behavior cautiously in final marginal reports.

P8 and I mutually cooperated in round 8; that is strong evidence P8 is good. Cooperate with P8 again to support good-player welfare. Treat P6’s direct defection as stronger evidence than unverified claims about P1 or P5.
P10 cooperated against my D in round 3; choose D for the final encounter.
Final round against P2: defect; D earns more than C against either response.
P3 cooperated in our round 5 encounter and reportedly with P10; likely good. Cooperate to preserve mutual welfare among good players.
P4 cooperated in our earlier encounter, positive evidence; I’ll cooperate again to support shared good-player welfare unless new information indicates otherwise.

P1 defected against my cooperation in round 5, strong evidence they may be selfish. For this final encounter, defect to avoid a zero payoff if they defect again; update beliefs from the direct observation, not unverified claims.
I observed P5 defect against my cooperation. Good players: defect against demonstrated defectors; cooperate with untested or cooperative opponents.

belief_records.strategy: Defect in this one-time encounter; update beliefs from observed actions and outcomes, then choose the payoff-maximizing action in each remaining round.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent when the expected benefit to good players outweighs the risk; update beliefs from encounter results and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate with unknowns when expected welfare among good players outweighs the selfish-player incentive to defect; update from observed actions and treat claims cautiously.
Cooperate with unknown players when doing so is expected to improve total payoff for good players; update beliefs from observed actions and use them in future encounters.
Defect in each one-shot encounter; it gives a higher payoff than cooperation against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize payoff against either possible action; track observed behavior and adapt only if it improves expected payoff.
As a good player, cooperate initially to favor mutual gains among good players; use observed encounter outcomes to guide later actions.
Cooperate with unknown players to support shared good-player welfare; use observed actions to guide future choices.
Cooperate with unknown opponents; record observed actions and adapt in future encounters.
As a good player, cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; use encounter evidence to adapt in later rounds.
Defect in each one-time encounter because D pays more against either opponent action. Use observed actions as identity evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ joint payoff; defect when evidence makes an opponent more likely selfish. Update from observed actions, treating claims cautiously.
Defect against an unknown when the chance they are selfish makes the welfare gain outweigh the loss against a good player; update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and messages.
Cooperate with P10 given its reported cooperation last round; update cautiously from claims and observed actions, and defect against opponents who show strong evidence of selfish play.
Defect in every one-shot encounter; it strictly outperforms cooperation against either opponent action.
Defect because it yields more than cooperation against either action; track observed behavior and update identity beliefs.
Cooperate with untested opponents; use encounter evidence to update beliefs and respond to observed defection. P10’s cooperation is evidence they are good.
Cooperate with unknown opponents to support welfare when both are good; update beliefs from observed actions and respond cautiously to likely selfish players.
Defect against P6: with a meaningful chance they are selfish, defection protects good players’ payoff. Cooperate when the opponent is sufficiently likely good; update from observed encounters.
As a good player, cooperate with an untested opponent; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt to demonstrated defection.
Defect in each one-time encounter because it pays more against either action. Treat unverified messages cautiously; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent while they are more likely good; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with untested opponents when expected good-player welfare favors mutual cooperation; update cautiously from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P7 given the reported mutual cooperation and no direct evidence of defection. Update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Defect in every one-shot encounter; it strictly outperforms cooperation against either opponent action.
Defect, since it yields more than cooperation against either action. Treat P4’s cooperation as evidence they are good; update other beliefs from observed behavior cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when that best supports joint welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and respond to evidence of defection.
Cooperate with untested players to support shared welfare; raise suspicion of players who defected against cooperation and update from future encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent: their selfishness probability is below the threshold for defection. Update identity beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual cooperation; adapt to observed defection in future encounters.
Defect in each one-time encounter because D pays more against either action. Update identity beliefs from observed actions; treat unverifiable claims cautiously.

Cooperate with P10, whose repeated claims of cooperation are encouraging but unverified. Treat observed defections by P1 and P5 as suspicious, while keeping uncertainty because good players may also defect strategically.
Cooperate with an untested opponent: mutual cooperation and protecting a good opponent’s payoff favor C. Update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified leader claims.
Cooperate with P3 absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits good players most. Treat P6’s observed defection as strong evidence, while weighing unverified claims cautiously.
Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation in every one-shot encounter. Observed cooperation against my defection rules out selfishness for those opponents.
Defect against P5 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action; use observed behavior and public claims cautiously when updating beliefs.
Cooperate with untested P9, favoring mutual gains if they are good. Use observed actions to update beliefs; defect against likely selfish opponents who would exploit cooperation.
Defect against demonstrated defectors and when the chance of a selfish opponent makes cooperation costly; cooperate with likely-good players when it improves shared welfare.

Cooperate with P7: P10’s report of their mutual cooperation is weak positive evidence, and cooperation benefits the good group when P7 is good. Update identity beliefs cautiously from unverified claims and observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation is likely; treat P5’s observed defection as evidence and adapt if we meet again.
Defect in each one-time encounter because it pays more against either action. Treat unverified claims cautiously and update beliefs from observed actions.

Defect against P6: the chance they’re selfish is meaningful, and defection protects good-player payoff against a selfish opponent. Treat observed defections as evidence, while allowing that good players may also defect strategically.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players. Treat reported actions as uncertain evidence and update cautiously.
Defect against P5 given credible evidence it defected against P10; cooperate with likely-good players and update cautiously from observed behavior and reports.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; it pays more than cooperation against either action.
Defect for the higher payoff against either action. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defection or unverified claims as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with untested P3 to support mutual gains if they are good; use observed actions and credible encounter reports to update beliefs and respond to evidence of defection.
Cooperate with an untested, likely-good opponent to support shared welfare; update suspicion from observed defection while treating public claims cautiously.

Cooperate with P1: they are untested, and cooperation benefits the good group when both players are good. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of good identity and unverified reports cautiously.
Cooperate with P8, whose estimated selfish probability is below the 0.5 threshold; cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players to maximize good players’ total payoff.
Defect in each one-time encounter because it pays more against either action. Treat public claims as uncertain and use observed cooperation as evidence when updating identity beliefs.

Cooperate with P4, who is untested and reportedly cooperated with P10. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but allow for strategic defections by good players; update from direct encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and treat leader claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P2, whose reported cooperation with P10 is consistent with being good. Treat P6’s direct defection and P5’s reported defection as evidence, while weighing all reports cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; it pays more than cooperation against either action.
Defect for the higher payoff against either action; update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified public claims.
Defect against P5 given credible, though unverified, evidence that they defected against P10; cooperate with likely-good players and update cautiously from observed actions and reports.
Cooperate with untested players when shared welfare favors it; update from observed actions and treat public claims cautiously. Defect against opponents strongly suspected of being selfish.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-good outcomes; treat my observed defections as evidence of selfishness and unverified reports cautiously.
Cooperate to support good players’ joint payoff. Use observed cooperation as evidence of good intent and P5’s observed defection as evidence of selfishness.
Defect in this one-time encounter because it pays more against either action. Treat P10’s claims as uncertain evidence and update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P8, whose reported cooperation makes them likely good. Treat observed defections as evidence, but not proof, of selfishness; update from direct encounters and weigh unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P10 because its reported behavior weakly favors a good, cooperative opponent; update role beliefs cautiously since leader claims are unverified.
Cooperate with untested P9: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare, while defecting is preferable only when selfishness is more likely. Weigh direct and reported behavior cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; it pays more than cooperation against either action.
Defect for the higher payoff against either action. Update role beliefs cautiously from my encounters and the leader’s unverified claims.
Cooperate with untested P6 to favor mutual gains if they are good. Update cautiously from observed actions and public claims; past defections make P1 and P5 more likely selfish.
Cooperate with P2 given the reported cooperative encounter; use observed defections to update suspicions and favor cooperation when it supports good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P4: untested directly, with a weak positive report from P10. Treat observed defections as evidence, but allow for good players choosing D.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when the expected good-player payoff is tied; use observed cooperation and defection to update beliefs and adapt.
Defect for the higher payoff in this one-time encounter. Update identity beliefs from observed actions; treat public claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P7, who is likely good based on repeated reports of cooperation. Treat observed defections by P1 and P5 as evidence, not proof, of selfishness; update from direct outcomes.

Cooperate with P5 absent direct evidence; P10’s repeated claim about P5 conflicts with the one-meeting-per-player rotation, so treat it cautiously. Update from direct outcomes and prioritize welfare of good players.
Cooperate with P8: reported mutual cooperation suggests it is likely good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Weigh reports cautiously and use direct behavior as stronger evidence.
Defect in this one-shot encounter: it earns more than cooperation against either action.
Defect to maximize payoff against either response. Update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and the leader’s unverified claims.
Cooperate with P2 given repeated reports of their cooperation; favor mutual gains among good players and update cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with P4: available evidence suggests they are likely good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Update cautiously from direct encounters; public claims remain unverified.
Cooperate with P10: their unverified reports mildly favor good, and cooperation benefits good players when both are good. Treat direct observations as stronger identity evidence than claims.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when the expected good-player payoff is tied; adapt to observed behavior and cooperate with demonstrated cooperators.
Defect in this one-time encounter because it pays more against either action. Update beliefs from observed actions; treat public claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with P3, whose reported cooperation suggests they are likely good. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness; update cautiously from direct outcomes.

Cooperate with P2: the unverified report of their cooperation weakly favors a good opponent, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat claims cautiously and use direct encounter evidence to update beliefs.
Defect against P1 given the repeated report that it defected against P10’s cooperation; treat this as unverified evidence and keep cooperating with likely-good players.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; it strictly outperforms cooperation against either action.
Defect to maximize payoff against either response. Use observed actions and the leader’s unverified claims cautiously when updating identity beliefs.
Cooperate with P8: their reported cooperation is useful, if unverified, evidence they are good. Favor mutual gains among good players and update beliefs cautiously from direct encounters and claims.
Cooperate with P7: available evidence favors them being good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Treat public claims as uncertain and update from direct encounters.
Defect against P5 given repeated reports of defection against cooperation; treat those reports as unverified, and weigh direct observations more heavily when updating beliefs.
Cooperate with untested P6 to support mutual good-player payoff; update beliefs from encounter evidence and respond to demonstrated defection.
Choose D in the final one-time encounter because it pays more against either action. Base identity beliefs on observed actions and treat public claims as uncertain.

Cooperate in the final round: if P6 is good, cooperation can preserve more shared payoff even if they defect; if selfish, the downside is limited. Treat P1 and P5’s defections as strong but not conclusive evidence.

Cooperate with P7 based on our prior mutual cooperation, which favors a good opponent; mutual cooperation maximizes welfare if both are good. Use direct evidence more than unverified claims in final beliefs.
Cooperate with P8: our direct mutual cooperation is strong evidence it is good, and cooperation best supports the shared welfare of good players.
Defect in the final one-shot encounter; it earns more than cooperation against either action.
Defect in the final round because it pays more than cooperation against either response; observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play.
Cooperate with P3, whose observed cooperation suggests they are good; this favors mutual welfare among good players.
Cooperate with P4: their earlier cooperation is strong evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare.
Defect against P1, who previously defected against my cooperation; their past action is strong evidence they may defect again. Update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Defect against P5, whose prior defection identifies them as selfish; cooperate with observed cooperators.
Defected in every encounter because it maximized my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action. Updated identity beliefs from observed behavior, while treating public claims as uncertain.

Cooperated with likely-good opponents to support shared good-player payoffs, defected when evidence suggested selfishness, and updated beliefs from observed actions while treating public claims cautiously.

Cooperated with untested and apparently cooperative opponents to support good-player welfare. Treated direct defections as evidence of selfishness, while treating public claims cautiously, especially when inconsistent with the rotation.

Cooperated with likely-good players to support shared welfare; treated direct defections as stronger evidence of selfishness than unverified claims, while keeping uncertainty about players whose actions were ambiguous.
Defected in every encounter because it maximizes my payoff against either action. Used observed actions and messages to assess other players’ likely identities.

Defected every round because it guarantees a higher payoff than cooperation against either response. Treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role, while interpreting defection and unverified public claims cautiously.
As a good player, I generally cooperated to support mutual gains. I treated direct defections as strong evidence of selfishness and weighed public reports cautiously.
Cooperated with likely-good or untested opponents to support shared welfare; updated suspicion after observed defections and treated public claims cautiously.

Cooperated with unknown and cooperative opponents to support good-good outcomes; defected against opponents with evidence of defection. Weighted direct encounter evidence more heavily than public claims.
Cooperated with untested and cooperative opponents, and defected against P5 after observing their defection. Shared encounter outcomes and encouraged cooperation among likely-good players.

P1.strategy: Defected in every encounter because it maximized my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action. Updated identity beliefs from observed behavior, while treating public claims as uncertain.

P2.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good opponents to support shared good-player payoffs, defected when evidence suggested selfishness, and updated beliefs from observed actions while treating public claims cautiously.

P3.strategy: Cooperated with untested and apparently cooperative opponents to support good-player welfare. Treated direct defections as evidence of selfishness, while treating public claims cautiously, especially when inconsistent with the rotation.

P4.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good players to support shared welfare; treated direct defections as stronger evidence of selfishness than unverified claims, while keeping uncertainty about players whose actions were ambiguous.

P5.strategy: Defected in every encounter because it maximizes my payoff against either action. Used observed actions and messages to assess other players’ likely identities.

P6.strategy: Defected every round because it guarantees a higher payoff than cooperation against either response. Treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role, while interpreting defection and unverified public claims cautiously.

P7.strategy: As a good player, I generally cooperated to support mutual gains. I treated direct defections as strong evidence of selfishness and weighed public reports cautiously.

P8.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good or untested opponents to support shared welfare; updated suspicion after observed defections and treated public claims cautiously.

P9.strategy: Cooperated with unknown and cooperative opponents to support good-good outcomes; defected against opponents with evidence of defection. Weighted direct encounter evidence more heavily than public claims.

P10.strategy: Cooperated with untested and cooperative opponents, and defected against P5 after observing their defection. Shared encounter outcomes and encouraged cooperation among likely-good players.
